   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.

evidence_quotes.quote: © The Author 2017. Development Policy Review © 2017 Overseas Development Institute
sample of 90 kiosks was selected, with 44 from Nyalenda A, 28 from Nyalenda B
There were 46 water samples taken from various sources: eight from randomly selected water kiosks,
The reported average price of a 20-litre jerrican of water was 3.01 Kenyan shillings (KSh)
81.4% of respondents said that water supply was not reliable; in Nyalenda B, 86.7% said it was
the operators had rented kiosk premises and lease arrangements prevented them installing tanks.

country.comment: The empirical study was conducted in three informal settlements (Nyalenda A, Nyalenda B, and Manyatta B) in the city of Kisumu, Kenya.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 4, Sections 1.3 & 2

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative comparisons use unadjusted one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD post-hoc tests across the two DMM settlements (Nyalenda A and B) and one non-DMM control settlement (Manyatta B); no 95% confidence intervals are reported in the paper.
effect_estimate.value: Under the Delegated Management Model (DMM), where municipal utility KIWASCO supplies subsidized bulk water to master-operators who co-set tariffs with kiosk operators (capping prices at KSh 3.00 per 20-litre jerrican vs up to KSh 5.00 at non-DMM kiosks and KSh 20 from vendors), mean kiosk water prices (N = 294 customers) were significantly lower in DMM slums Nyalenda B (KSh 3.01) and Nyalenda A (KSh 3.07) than in non-DMM control slum Manyatta B (KSh 3.60; F(2, 291) = 14.41, p < .01). Mean monthly household water expenditure was also significantly lower in Nyalenda B (KSh 485.42) and Nyalenda A (KSh 604.73) than in Manyatta B (KSh 665.90; F(2, 291) = 5.12, p < .01). Average customers queuing per kiosk were 2.8 (SD = 2.1) in Nyalenda B, 1.9 (SD = 1.1) in Nyalenda A, and 1.1 (SD = 1.3) in Manyatta B (F(2, 100) = 3.63, p < 0.05; significant between Nyalenda B and Manyatta B), while container counts did not differ significantly (7.9, 4.8, and 6.3; F(2, 100) = 1.1, p = .33). Service reliability remained poor across all settlements—81.4% in Nyalenda A, 86.7% in Nyalenda B, and 93.3% in Manyatta B reported unreliable supply over the prior 6 months, with kiosks open 11.6 hours/day on average experiencing 3.3 hours/day of disruption—exacerbated by main-line outages, pipe bursts, and landlord lease restrictions barring rented kiosk operators from installing storage tanks. Microbiological testing (N = 46 samples) detected zero total coliforms or E. coli in all 8 kiosk samples, whereas 100% of vendor, well, and spring samples (16/16) tested positive for both, and 11/22 household storage samples had total coliforms (5/22 E. coli) due to household recontamination and use of unsafe alternative sources during outages.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 6–10, Sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 & 3.7; Table 1, PDF p. 10

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling under MMAT is 2 (even if viewed as a non-randomized intervention comparison, unadjusted post-only comparison of 2 DMM slums vs 1 control slum without baseline data would have Serious/Critical confounding risk). Assigned 2 because the study empirically observes and documents how DMM institutional delegation, collaborative bulk/kiosk tariff governance, and landlord lease restrictions on non-owned premises operate on water affordability, reliability, and water quality.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 3–4, Sections 1.2–1.3; PDF pp. 6–11, Sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.6 & 4

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines DMM utility-resident institutional partnership and bulk/kiosk service accommodation in informal settlements (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, accommodation, participation), bulk subsidies, regulated vs unregulated kiosk tariffs, and operator capital/lease costs (BURDEN, fees), historical informal-settlement illegality, absentee landlord consent, and lease prohibitions against extending pipes or installing storage tanks on rented land plus unplanned settlement layouts (ELIGIBILITY, tenure, property, planning), and pipe vandalism/theft sanctions, customer hygiene complaints, and missing public-health regulatory enforcement (ENFORCEMENT, sanction, complaint).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, tenure, property, planning, fees, accommodation, complaint, sanction, participation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 2–4, Sections 1.1–1.2; PDF pp. 6–11, Sections 3.3, 3.4, 3.6 & 4

outcome_flags.comment: Measures access to improved/safe kiosk water vs unsafe alternative sources (water_access), price per 20L jerrican and monthly household water expenditure (affordability), 6-month supply availability satisfaction (service_reliability), daily hours of supply interruption/outage (service_continuity), E. coli/coliform water quality and kiosk hygiene (service_quality), and container counts / sufficiency of kiosk water for household needs (service_quantity).
outcome_flags.value: water_access, affordability, service_reliability, service_continuity, service_quality, service_quantity
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 5–10, Sections 2.1, 2.3, 3.1, 3.3–3.7 & 4; Table 1, PDF p. 10

publication_year.comment: The article PDF itself explicitly prints 2017 in the running header, copyright line, and 'How to cite this article' block (Early View publication prior to 2018 issue pagination). Extracted strictly from the printed document text per codebook rules.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, header & copyright notice; PDF p. 13, 'How to cite this article'

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Selected MMAT because the study combines primary quantitative components (structured customer survey N = 294, queue/container counts, one-way ANOVA across two DMM slums and one non-DMM control slum, and laboratory microbiological testing of 46 water samples) with primary qualitative components (semi-structured interviews with open-ended questions and participant observations at water kiosks and 22 households). Lacks pre-intervention baseline or quasi-experimental econometric identification (e.g., DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS) for ROBINS-I.

sample_size.comment: Note minor arithmetic/reporting discrepancy in the paper: Section 2.1 states 'A random sample of 90 kiosks was selected, with 44 from Nyalenda A, 28 from Nyalenda B, and 25 from Manyatta B' (44 + 28 + 25 = 97), and Section 3.1 reports F(2, 100) for kiosk-level comparisons. Customer survey N = 294 (109 + 107 + 78 = 294, matching F(2, 291) in Section 3.3). Microbiological water sample N = 46 across sources, including 22 household storage samples (10 Nyalenda A, 8 Nyalenda B, 4 Manyatta B). Semi-structured interviews with kiosk operators were also conducted, with exact operator N not stated in this article.
sample_size.value: 3 informal settlements in Kisumu; 294 water kiosk customers interviewed (109 in Nyalenda A, 107 in Nyalenda B, 78 in Manyatta B) across a reported random sample of 90 water kiosks (printed breakdown: 44 in Nyalenda A, 28 in Nyalenda B, 25 in Manyatta B); 46 water samples for microbiological analysis (8 water kiosks, 4 water vendors, 4 protected wells, 4 covered wells, 4 protected springs, and 22 household storage containers)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 1.3; PDF p. 5, Sections 2.1 & 2.3; Table 1, PDF p. 10

study_design.comment: Post-implementation comparative cross-sectional study conducted in May–June 2013 comparing two DMM settlements (Nyalenda A and B) with one adjacent non-DMM control settlement (Manyatta B), integrating structured survey questionnaires analyzed via percentages and one-way ANOVA, semi-structured open-ended interview questions, participant observations at kiosks and households, and membrane-filtration microbiological water testing.
study_design.value: Comparative cross-sectional mixed-methods case study (semi-structured customer and operator interviews/questionnaires with one-way ANOVA, participant observation, and microbiological water-quality testing comparing two DMM slums and one non-DMM control slum)
